newsitem.title: INDIA: India's falling export growth a policy concern - RBI.
newsitem.headline: India's falling export growth a policy concern - RBI.

text.p: India's declining rate of export growth has emerged as an area of policy concern, a senior official of the country's central bank said on Friday.

"The deceleration in export growth during 1996/97 has emerged as an area of policy concern and exchange rate is often blamed for that," Deputy Governor Y.V. Reddy of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) told a meeting of forex dealers.

Reddy said the slowdown in export growth could equally well be attributed to the decline in world trade coupled with the sluggishness in manufacturing goods' prices in the global market, variations in cross-currency rates exchange rates and deceleration in domestic industrial activities.
"However, we should accept that beyond a point, real appreciation of a currency can hurt exports," he added.
Global investment bank Merrill Lynch said in its August India report that the strong rupee was hurting Indian exports.

"Exports grew at only four percent in FY 1996/97 (April-March) against an 18 percent average growth rate for the previous three years," Merrill's report said. "The real appreciation of the rupee is having a negative impact on exports."
The rupee has remained steady at 35.70/80 against the dollar for the past one year.
